claims.statement: A list of objects does not by itself identify their actions or spatial relationships; a whole-image answer must address the relation/action actually asked about.

evidence.supports: VQA abilities and annotations distinguish objects, attributes, activities and relations; shortcuts/object recognition alone do not establish scene understanding.

claims.scope: Task distinction, not a claim of measured course model capability or that every caption must mention every relation.

claims.statement: A still image does not guarantee knowledge of unseen before/after events or history.

evidence.supports: Distinguishes grounded scene questions from speculative events that may lead to or result from the depicted scene.
Multiple different histories can yield the same still image, so the observed image alone cannot uniquely establish one history.

claims.scope: Limits of visually supported evidence; external context or prior knowledge may provide additional information but is not contained in the toy picture.

evidence.supports: Positions and learned spatial relations are distinct requirements of an image-sequence model.

claims.scope: Noninjectivity of this representation; additional input/context may support a guess. Does not claim that every averaging configuration loses this distinction.

claims.statement: Natural-photo relation/action tasks require suitable learning and validation examples; increasing color labels alone does not guarantee learning holding, left/right or activity answers.

evidence.locator: Introduction and section 2, pp.6700-6702; sections 3/3.1, pp.6702-6703
evidence.supports: Distinguishes real-image diversity and relation reasoning from constrained synthetic object/attribute tasks; constructs grounded relation-rich questions.
Multimodal pre-training plus actual VQA task fine-tuning is distinct from raw pixel retention.
Same color labels for different relation targets fail to specify a unique relation answer under a color-only objective.

claims.scope: Course supervised-task guidance and lack of guarantee, not an assertion that explicit relation labels are the only way to learn or that pretrained models know no relations.

claims.statement: Object detection can identify objects using rectangular bounding boxes, whose locations supply spatial clues.

evidence.supports: Predicted boxes have [x1,y1,x2,y2] coordinates plus labels and scores.
Scene-graph objects have boxes specifying position/size, with separate relation edges.

claims.scope: Existence of box-based detectors; positions alone do not prove semantic interactions, intentions or scene history.

claims.statement: Whole-image question answering can use a sequence of image patches and learn from positional information instead of first requiring object boxes.

evidence.locator: Figure 1; section 3.1 equation (1) and inductive-bias paragraph, pp.3-4
evidence.supports: Patch sequence with position embeddings, spatial relations learned rather than innate.
Direct image-patch/text sequence is used for actual VQAv2 image-question task fine-tuning without region supervision.

claims.scope: Published architecture possibility; retaining sequence or adding position embeddings by itself guarantees no relationship understanding or course-model quality.

evidence.supports: First cell loses red 0.5 and second gains red 0.5.
